text:
elaine_cs: @marc_oncall Cobalt-Analytics (ded-res-1823) reporting a sudden p99 tail spike since ~2026-03-16 02:03 UTC. p95 steady ~220ms but p99 jumping to 3.2s and occasional 8s. They started a large batch embeddings job. Ticket #5482 — can we triage?

sre-bot: ALERT: tenant=cobalt-analytics p99_latency > 2s (last 5m). nodes affected: node-12,node-15. link: https://console.redwood/alerts/5482 :rotating_light:

marc_oncall: ack. tagging infra/runtime. any quick mitigations we can apply while we dig in? :eyes:

maya_support: I asked the customer for repro steps. They sent back the exact curl and parameters. posting below.

maya_support: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUST_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":["..."],"batch_size":512,"concurrency":8}'
```

maya_support: Customer says they run 8 concurrent workers with batch_size=512 for a 2M-row job.

felix_runtime: thanks. initial look at runtime traces shows heavy KV cache miss rate for that tenant and lots of scheduling queueing on node-12. pattern: large batches -> long tokenization + memory pressure -> queue head-of-line. logs: 

felix_runtime: ```
[2026-03-16T02:04:12Z] tenant=cobalt-analytics req_id=abcd1234 latency_ms=3200 stage=serve kv_cache_hit=false queue_ms=2100 node=node-12
[2026-03-16T02:04:21Z] tenant=cobalt-analytics req_id=abcd1235 latency_ms=8100 stage=serve reason=overloaded-shard node=node-12
```

ingrid_infra: confirmed node-12 gpu_util=92% and queue_len spikes coincident with their job windows. I'm seeing "overloaded-shard" and OOM-retry traces on the shard that hosts their model variant.

felix_runtime: short-term mitigations:
- cap per-tenant concurrency to 4 (their current 8)
- apply soft qps throttle for tenant key (eg qps=250)
- create a 30-60m ephemeral reservation routed to a less-loaded GPU pool (res-1823-ephem) to isolate noisy workload
- optionally route their workload to a quantized variant (gptq-4-10b) to drop per-token latency

marc_oncall: sounds good. can infra create the ephem reservation and support apply the concurrency cap? I'll craft the change.

maya_support: created internal change:
- per-tenant max_concurrency=4 for key=cobalt-analytics (soft enforcement)
- qps_limit=250 (burst allowed)
- created reservation res-1823-ephem (2x A100-equivalent) active for 45m starting 2026-03-16T02:12Z -> owner=maya_support
- added tenant to short-term burst allowlist so routing will prefer res-1823-ephem

maya_support: applied changes at 02:12 UTC. notifying customer.

elaine_cs: customer reports immediate improvement in their dashboard, p99 dropped from ~3.2s to ~420ms within 3 minutes after routing to res-1823-ephem. they confirm job continues but will throttle client-side too. :thumbsup:

marc_oncall: great. leaving the reservation for 45m to finish their batch, but we should follow up with a sustained plan: recommend smaller batch_size or adaptive batching, prefix caching warm-up, and model quantization guidance.

felix_runtime: I also opened a bug to improve per-tenant queue fairness: when KV cache miss rate > 60% for large batches, we should trigger automatic concurrency backpressure and suggest quantized model. ref: INF-RUN-764.

ingrid_infra: we'll keep node-12 monitored and migrate shards if we see repeated noisy patterns.

maya_support: ticket updated and customer notified. they asked for a short doc with recommended settings — I'll draft and send.

elaine_cs: nice quick win. closing this escalation once post-checks are green. follow-up items: optimize-recommendation for embeddings, consider a reservation autoscale for large batch jobs, and add a troubleshooting snippet to support KB.

marc_oncall: agreed. if p99 creeps up again reopen. adding to weekly postmortem agenda.

sre-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: alert 5482 auto-cleared after routing change (p99 < 500ms for 10m).
